answer.line: Yeast run alcoholic fermentation: pyruvate gives off CO2, which lifts the dough, and ends as ethanol, which bakes off.

steps: Name the pathway. Yeast without oxygen run alcoholic fermentation.
Pyruvate loses CO2 and becomes acetaldehyde. That gas is what lifts the dough.
Acetaldehyde takes the electrons from NADH and becomes ethanol. NAD+ goes back to glycolysis, and the ethanol bakes off.

choices.note: Lactate fermentation runs in muscle and some bacteria, and it releases no gas. Nothing would lift the dough.
CO2 lifts the dough; ethanol bakes off.
The link reaction also strips CO2 from pyruvate, but it makes acetyl-CoA and needs oxygen downstream. Fermentation ends in ethanol.
Pyruvate is where glycolysis ends and fermentation starts. And yeast give off no hydrogen gas.
Ethanol holds, but fermentation neither uses nor makes oxygen. The gas in the dough is CO2.

lockIt: Yeast fermentation: pyruvate to CO2 plus ethanol. Muscle: pyruvate to lactate, no gas.
